evidence_type: Author-constructed instructional resource; no new classroom observations
judgment_scope: Support, refutation or non-establishment relative to the named source context, not global truth

pairs.supported: The reported DPR retriever uses two independent BERT encoders for questions and passages.
pairs.challenge: The reported DPR retriever shares one BERT encoder parameter set between questions and passages.
pairs.rationale: The architecture description explicitly specifies independent networks. Sharing the BERT architecture does not entail sharing one parameter set.
pairs.repair: Restore the distinction between the question encoder and the passage encoder.
pairs.review_status: AI-assisted source inspection; no independent human annotation

pairs.supported: The BART paper compares its bidirectional encoder with BERT within a broader sequence-to-sequence architecture.
pairs.challenge: BART is initialized by loading a released BERT checkpoint.
pairs.rationale: The comparison concerns architecture. The model section separately specifies random parameter initialization, rather than BERT checkpoint initialization.
pairs.repair: Describe the architectural comparison without asserting checkpoint reuse.
pairs.review_status: AI-assisted source inspection; no independent human annotation

pairs.supported: T5 describes its baseline denoising objective as inspired by BERT masked language modelling and word dropout.
pairs.challenge: T5 describes BERT as the sole inspiration for its baseline denoising objective.
pairs.rationale: The sentence crosses a page boundary and names a second influence. Reading only its first page drops a consequential part of the statement.
pairs.repair: Retain both named influences and restrict the claim to the baseline objective.
pairs.review_status: AI-assisted source inspection; no independent human annotation

pairs.supported: RAG initializes its retriever from DPR and keeps the document encoder fixed during its reported fine-tuning.
pairs.challenge: RAG fine-tunes both the DPR question encoder and the document encoder in its reported training procedure.
pairs.rationale: Initialization and subsequent training are different claims. The training subsection identifies the fixed document encoder.
pairs.repair: Separate initialization from fine-tuning and preserve which encoder stays fixed.
pairs.review_status: AI-assisted source inspection; no independent human annotation

pairs.supported: RAG uses a BART-large generator and fine-tunes that generator in the reported procedure.
pairs.challenge: RAG keeps its BART generator parameters fixed throughout the reported fine-tuning.
pairs.rationale: The generator and training subsections identify both the component and its update policy.
pairs.repair: State that the generator is fine-tuned; do not transfer the document encoder policy to it.
pairs.review_status: AI-assisted source inspection; no independent human annotation

pairs.supported: FiD reports DPR retrieval for Natural Questions and TriviaQA, and BM25 for SQuAD.
pairs.challenge: FiD uses DPR for every dataset reported in the paper.
pairs.rationale: The SQuAD configuration supplies an explicit counterexample to the universal statement.
pairs.classroom_connection: The overgeneralisation is described in the practitioner account; these card wordings are authored paraphrases, not student quotations.
pairs.review_status: AI-assisted source inspection; no independent human annotation

pairs.supported: The reported FiD experiments initialize from T5; the method description also allows a model such as BART.
pairs.challenge: The FiD method requires T5 and excludes BART as a possible sequence-to-sequence model.
pairs.rationale: The method explicitly gives another possible model. An experimental instantiation is not an architectural requirement.
pairs.repair: Keep the T5 initialization claim within the scope of the reported experiments.
pairs.review_status: AI-assisted source inspection; no independent human annotation

pairs.supported: The FiD paper compares its handling of retrieved passages with RAG and describes joint processing in the decoder.
pairs.challenge: The comparison establishes that FiD loads a previously trained RAG system as a component.
pairs.rationale: The comparison and method description do not establish the asserted component inheritance. Withhold that claim; a comparison is not a lineage record.
pairs.repair: Retain the processing comparison. To assert reuse, obtain explicit implementation or initialization evidence.
pairs.review_status: AI-assisted source inspection; no independent human annotation

pairs.supported: T5 and BART can be compared as encoder-decoder approaches with denoising pre-training.
pairs.challenge: Their shared encoder-decoder and denoising properties establish that T5 historically influenced BART.
pairs.rationale: Shared properties support an analytical comparison. They do not supply evidence of the direction or existence of historical influence.
pairs.repair: Label the relation as a curator comparison; request a historical or author-attribution source before claiming influence.
pairs.review_status: AI-assisted source inspection; no independent human annotation
